summary.headline: Rupa Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6.3% to INR441.5 crore on 9% volume growth, while FY26 EBITDA fell 11.6% to INR115.3 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6.3% YoY to INR441.5 crore, with volume up 9%, and EBITDA rose 19.8% to INR55 crore as margin expanded 150 bps to 12.5%, helped by Athleisure mix. For full-year FY26, revenue grew only 1.6% to INR1,259.1 crore while EBITDA and PAT declined 11.6% and 12.9%, with margins compressed. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-12% (largely volume-led) and EBITDA margin of 9-10%, and announced a 4-5% price hike in April with a further 2-3% possible in June-July. Management flagged intense price competition, crude-linked raw material costs, freight and FX pressures from the Middle East disruption.

segments.name: Athleisure
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume grew 20% and value grew 25% YoY; management credited it as the main driver of the gross margin improvement.

segments.name: Channels (exports / modern trade incl. e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Exports were 3% and modern trade including e-commerce 5% of FY26 revenue; management says all channels, including GT, modern trade, exports and e-commerce, need equal focus.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-12%, split roughly equally between volume (4-5%) and value/price (4-5%).
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9-10%, versus 9.2% in FY26.
FY27 advertisement spend guided at 6-7% of revenue, versus about 4% in Q4 FY26.
Price hike of 4-5% taken in April 2026; a further 2-3% possible in June-July 2026 depending on market conditions.
Management targets profitability improvement of about 50 bps YoY each year over the next couple of years, alongside 10-12% growth.
Gross margin of about 28% in Q4 expected to be sustained with the initial price hike, per management.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex outlay of INR60 crore over two years to develop manufacturing-cum-warehousing facilities at Hosiery Park, Kolkata, West Bengal.
Phase 3 investment in sales and distribution network made during the quarter.
Recently appointed all-India sales head, strategy and EBO heads, a separate e-commerce head and four zonal heads, all in place for about a month as of the call.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 volume growth of 9%, but revenue growth remained modest because of intense industry price competition.
Trade discount intensity is around 12%, and management expects to maintain the same level of discount.
Management described the market as a buyer's market and said discounts will be given in line with the market.
Inventory split: raw material about 13%, finished goods about 54%, work in progress about 33%.
Brand and development spend of about INR70 crore in FY26: outdoor about 50%, television 10-12%, print about 12%, digital about 4%; the remaining share was not broken down.
Management said the company is shifting focus from primary to secondary (distributor-to-retailer) sales and will maintain optimum channel inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR60 crore outlay over two years for manufacturing-cum-warehousing facilities at Hosiery Park, Kolkata, West Bengal, to strengthen in-house capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Advertisement spend in Q4 and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 advertisement spend was about 4% of revenue; FY27 guidance is 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the US-Iran war and Middle East disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct impact on the business, but flagged higher crude-linked raw material prices, higher shipping and freight costs, and FX volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Price hikes taken and planned?
qa_highlights.answer: A 4-5% price hike in April and possibly another 2-3% in June-July, depending on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher gross margin driven by product mix, with Athleisure growing strongly in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term roadmap given low historical growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 10-12% growth for the next couple of years, with profitability rising about 50 bps YoY, driven by secondary and retail focus and a new retail team.

risks_watch: Price competition: management says pricing remains intense and any further price hikes depend on market conditions and yarn/cotton prices.
Input cost and logistics: higher crude-linked raw material costs, freight costs from shipping disruption, and FX volatility from the Middle East situation.
Sustainability of the Q4 gross margin (about 28%) and 12.5% EBITDA margin, given that management attributes much of it to Athleisure mix and initial price hikes.
FY27 guidance of 10-12% growth requires about 4-5% volume growth, versus 1.6% revenue growth in FY26.
Advertisement spend rising to 6-7% of revenue in FY27 from about 4% in Q4, which could pressure margins against the 9-10% EBITDA guidance.
Brand spend breakdown incomplete (about 20% unaccounted) and promised separately; new sales team impact not yet proven.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the forward plan and the new sales team but cautious on pricing, repeatedly saying outcomes depend on market conditions and yarn and cotton prices. Several answers on gross margin sustainability and discounting were hedged, and some detail (brand spend breakdown, pricing outlook) was deferred.
